title: Düzensiz fiiller: drive–drove–driven
explain_tr: Düzensiz fiillerin üç hâli vardır: **V1** (şimdiki), **V2** (geçmiş: *Yesterday I drove*), **V3** (have/had/be ile: *I have driven*, *It was driven*).

**V2** tek başına kullanılır: *I **went** home.* **V3** asla tek başına kullanılmaz; önünde **have / has / had** (Perfect) ya da **be** (edilgen) olmalı: *I **have gone**, The car **was driven**.* *I gone* ✗, *I have went* ✗.

Benzer görünen kelimelere dikkat: **drive** (araba sürmek) – drove – driven, düzensiz. **derive** (türetmek, elde etmek) – derived – derived, düzenli. *The word is **derived** from Latin.* / *She **drove** to work.*
Olumsuz ve soru cümlesinde geçmiş **did** ile gösterilir, fiil V1'e döner: *I **didn't go*** (✗ didn't went), *Did you **see** it?* (✗ Did you saw).
explain_en: Irregular verbs have three forms: V1 (base), V2 (past simple), V3 (past participle). V3 always needs have/has/had or be.
Do not confuse drive–drove–driven (irregular) with derive–derived–derived (regular). After did / didn't use V1.

pairs.wrong: I have drove this car for ten years.
pairs.right: I have driven this car for ten years.

pairs.wrong: I didn't went to work on Monday.
pairs.right: I didn't go to work on Monday.

pairs.wrong: This data is drived from the survey.
pairs.right: This data is derived from the survey.

exercises.explain_tr: "yesterday" → Past Simple, lose–**lost**. (yesterday ile Present Perfect kullanılmaz.)
